persistedClaim.text: An SDM (Sub-Divisional Magistrate) officer's stamp is not accepted for Italian document attestation/apostille; only designated state officers can complete that step.

record.text: If you're looking at a master's degree to study at one of the top ranking eight universities of New Zealand, you need a CGPA of minimum 6.3. Backlogs are accepted in case of New Zealand if these backlogs are only in year one and year two, and we require an IELTS of 6.5, no band less than six, or equivalent in PTE, TOEFL, or Duolingo.

Ruby Thomas: Step three is basically where you then start doing certain procedures related to your academic certifications. Now, for Italy, we require that your previous academic documentations have certain stamps. This is very vital, and this has to be done on the original documentations. What is the first stamp? You have to get the first signature from the school, from the university—the principal, the registrar, whoever is the highest authority puts a stamp, their official stamp on the back side of the documentations. Number two: you get the state verification, HRD, from the state that you have graduated. Ministry of External Affairs has designated certain officers in each of the state. So it's not like any state officer, you just randomly go, they can do it. No, and definitely not an SDM officer. No SDM officer is allowed to put their stamp on the educational documentations. There are certain officers in each state which have been authorized to put a stamp on the back side of the educational documentation. This happens on the back side of the original documentations, not on photocopies. Once the state officer has put a stamp, you send your documents to the Ministry of External Affairs, who then put their stamp. So if you see the picture that's here, the colorful box that you can see, that is the Ministry of External Affairs stamp, the Apostille, and there is also a big square-like stamp which is done by the state officers also. These three levels of verification can be done only after a student has received an acceptance, not before it, because when you go to the state officer, they will ask for what purpose are you getting it done, so you have to proceed and show them the offer letter that needs to be presented. So please be very careful about this. Like I had said, an SDM officer cannot put a stamp. There are agencies who actually do this procedure, and they inform the students like it's very easy to get the SDM officer stamp, so why not just go ahead with it? We will not accept it. The student will face a lot of problem when he or she is applying for the visa. There is also one thing: certain universities will be like, "It's fine, we do not require these stamps, you can just come without them." Even if they say that, no, you require this as per the visa protocol; you have to get it done. It doesn't matter if you're going for like a semester exchange, a short-term program, for a long-term program; you still have to get it on the educational documentations, which is finally completed. So this is the third step that a student has to go. The faster you start this process the better, because the state-level verification takes time. There are some of the states that actually take even one month. So so as to not waste time and apply for your visa on time, it is important that you follow these steps as soon as you're able to get it done.
You don't even submit your passport because in case of New Zealand, you get an e-visa copy.

Ruby Thomas: Like I had said, you cannot get the attestation and apostille done from an SDM officer. There are certain designated officers in each state. So it's not like in every state it will be the educational officer. In Karnataka, for example, in Mysore specifically, the designated office is the land-related commissioner. It's not even an education office, but as per the Ministry, that is the designated office, so you have to go there. So this is also very important. Main important thing: the students will have to be sponsored either by themselves if they're working professionals, or by their parents, or you can take up an educational loan as well. You can show additional documents, FD, which will be considered an asset mostly, not like a main sponsor. Wrong jurisdiction is one of the most recurring mistakes and the things that are overlooked. You are from Rajasthan, you have been living in Mumbai for 6 months, you come back to Delhi and apply for the visa—no, you will have to apply from Mumbai. This is very important: you have to ensure that the students are correctly matching to their jurisdiction consulates and the Embassy.
